proof.criterion: R7 for asks: a link written in a question, an option or an answer starts at that part, is counted once, and reaches its issue's reference closure.
proof.surface: The same running Dispatch, over HTTP and through `dispatch read --issue`.
proof.command: Asks whose question, whose option alone and whose person-written answer alone name dispatch://CORE-16/artifact/<slug>, then GET /api/v1/references?to=<that document> and dispatch read --issue CORE-15 / CORE-17
proof.observed: A link in two options is two edges, one from each part (ask/<id>#b2 and ask/<id>#b3), and dropping the option that held one leaves the other alone. Where the question and an option both name the target, the edges are the two parts and no ask-level row: heldByABlock hides it. `dispatch read --issue` prints `CORE/odoc-1462930646 · depth 1 via ask <id>` for a document named only in an option, prints `- none` after that option is dropped, and prints the same line for a document named only in a person's answer. ask_block_refs.source_seq for the answer's edge is 12, not null, so a ?since= read of the target lists it.
proof.negativeControl: Before the answer was written the same issue's closure read `References: - none`, and the target's own backlinks held no ask edge; the line appears only with the write that creates the part.

proof.criterion: R11's reply clause: a reply in an ask's thread names the part it answers, and R10: a part the ask does not hold is refused by name.

proof.observed: b1 and b2 are 201, each answering with reply_block {node: ask/<id>#b1|#b2, ref: dispatch://CORE-10/ask/<id>#b-b1|#b-b2, text: the part's own text, removed: false}; GET ?to=<option>&kind=replies_to lists the replies that named it. A nested reply inside the ask's thread (reply_to=<a reply>, reply_to_block=b2) also names the ask's part. The CLI prints `Replied on ask <id> (comment <id>; ask now waiting on human)`.

proof.criterion: Recovery and concurrency of the part index: a build that wrote no parts is skipped rather than mis-resolved, a later write re-indexes, and concurrent edits leave one consistent revision.
proof.surface: The same running Dispatch, over HTTP, with the store read directly through psql.
proof.command: delete from ask_block_state/ask_blocks for one ask, then GET /api/v1/asks/<id> and ?to=<part>; then PATCH the ask; then `update ask_block_state set owed_at = now()` and PATCH again; separately, 12 concurrent PATCHes of one ask's options
proof.observed: With the part rows gone the ask reads revision: null with every option id null, ?to=<ask>&kind=part_of is empty and ?to=<part> is 404 naming the part — no row of another ask is resolved in its place. The next write re-indexes from revision 1 (b1..b4) and the owed_at a later write finds is cleared. The 12 concurrent edits all answered 200 and left parts_live=3, parts_total=3, dup_block_ids=0, ask_block_state.revision=13 and max(ask_blocks.changed_revision)=13.
proof.negativeControl: The deleted-rows state is itself the control for the index's recovery: the read before the re-indexing write answers 404 for the very part id that answered 200 a moment earlier, and no part of any other ask answers in its place.
